# Nobel Prize in Chemistry — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/nobel-prize-in-chemistry.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/nobel-prize-in-chemistry.ttl`](../decks/nobel-prize-in-chemistry.ttl) · **Cards:** 117 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

Every Nobel Prize in Chemistry from 1901 to 2025, one card per prize year: 117 cards with the year on the front and the laureate or laureates on the back, with a short note on what the prize was for. Years with no award are left out; the deck ends with the 2025 prize, as the 2026 prize had not been announced when the deck was made on 4 October 2026. From the Nobel Prize API and Wikidata, checked against NobelPrize.org. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the Nobel Foundation or the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.

## Licensing

The deck is CC0 1.0. Its content comes from two sources whose terms allow that: the Nobel Prize API, whose terms say the service is "free to use according to the Creative Commons Zero (CC0) license", and Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0. The selection (every prize year with an award), the laureates and their order, the English and most Swedish names, the facts in the notes and the motivations the notes paraphrase come from the API, cross-checked with Wikidata; the three Swedish forms and one English spelling that differ from the API come from Wikidata's labels. The notes are in the deck's own words. Two sources were used for verification only and contributed nothing but confirmation: NobelPrize.org's pages (copyright Nobel Prize Outreach: "You may not reproduce, distribute ... or otherwise use the Content without prior written permission"), read to confirm what the open sources give — the evidence quotes each year's one-sentence award statement from that year's summary page with the motivations elided, and the title and five-word motivation of the 2021 Swedish press release (short quotations, to show what was checked; the same facts are CC0 from the same maker through the API, and the quotes are in the provenance report, not on the cards), but no text, selection or data field was taken, which also keeps clear of the EU sui generis database right (Directive 96/9/EC) in the site as a whole; and the Swedish Wikipedia's table of laureates (CC BY-SA 4.0), compared with the Swedish names but not copied, its selection not used (copying the table would have made the deck CC BY-SA). The API terms say that, in case of conflict, they prevail over CC0, and they add conditions for applications: not to alter the data or mislead users — the deck changes the API's names in five documented places only (in English a trailing space removed and an accent restored; in Swedish three established forms of names: Semjonov, Prigogine and Heyrovský), and its notes summarise the official motivations without changing their meaning — and to credit the API as the data source, which the deck does. They also say applications may not use Nobel Prize Outreach's name or trademarks "in their titles or logos, or in any way that implies endorsement", and NobelPrize.org's terms of use say "you may not use the Nobel Foundation trademarks without prior written permission from the Nobel Foundation". The deck's title, "Nobel Prize in Chemistry" / "Nobelpriset i kemi", uses the prize's name only to say what the deck is about (descriptive use: there is no other way to name the subject), with no logo, medal or other Nobel graphics, and its description says it is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Nobel Foundation or the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. As for the literature and peace decks, whether that satisfies the API terms' "titles" clause is a judgement for the publisher, flagged for Anton Wiklund before release; the fallback is a title without the prize's name, such as "Chemistry laureates 1901–2025" / "Kemipristagare 1901–2025".

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. Prizes and selection. On 2026-10-04 the Nobel Prize API was queried for all Nobel Prizes in Chemistry (nobelPrizeCategory=che, sorted by year; see Queries) and for all chemistry laureates. It returned 125 prize years, 1901–2025, and 198 laureates (two of them with two chemistry prizes, so 200 laureate-years). Eight years have no laureates: 1916, 1917, 1919, 1924, 1933, 1940, 1941 and 1942; NobelPrize.org's summary page for each of them says "No Nobel Prize was awarded this year". They are left out. Each of the other 117 years became one card, with the year (the API's awardYear, the year the prize is for) on the front, tagged zxx as a number in no language.
3. Back: English. The laureates of each year, in the order the API lists them, joined with ", " and " and ". The English names are the API's knownName.en, the names under which the Nobel Foundation lists the laureates (titles such as Sir and Lord included: Sir William Ramsay, Lord Todd), unchanged except in two places: the API's "Aleksey Yekimov " has a trailing space, removed; and "Jaroslav Heyrovsky" is written "Jaroslav Heyrovský", his Czech name and Wikidata's English label (as the peace deck restored the accents of María Corina Machado and Óscar Arias Sánchez).
4. Back: Swedish. The same laureates joined with ", " and " och ". Each Swedish name is the API's knownName.se (from the laureates endpoint, see Queries; the nobelPrizes endpoint has English names only) unless Swedish has an established form that differs, taken from Wikidata's Swedish label (query 2) and confirmed by the Swedish Wikipedia's table of laureates (its link targets): Nikolaj Semjonov (API "Nikolaj Semjenov"), Ilya Prigogine (API "Ilja Prigozjin", a transliteration from Russian of the name of a Belgian chemist, who wrote it Prigogine) and Jaroslav Heyrovský (API "Jaroslav Heyrovsky"). Every other Swedish name is the API's, which for these laureates is the same as the English name.
5. Notes. Every card has a backNote saying briefly what the prize was for, written in the deck's own words from the API's English motivation (motivation.en) and, for the Swedish note, the API's Swedish motivation (motivation.se) where it is given and correct; the notes shorten the motivations, sometimes keeping their wording (for example the Swedish notes for 1987 and 2013); the API is CC0, so this needs no attribution. Where the laureates of one year were cited for different work, the note names each (for example 1912: "Grignard: … Sabatier: …"). Four notes add a fact about another Nobel Prize, each from the API's laureate records and Wikidata's P166: Marie Curie's earlier Physics Prize (1911), Linus Pauling's Peace Prize (1954), and Frederick Sanger's and K. Barry Sharpless's second chemistry prizes (1958/1980, 2001/2022). The API has no Swedish motivation for 2021 and a wrong one for 1958 (see Quality control); the Swedish note for 2021 was translated for this deck, its term confirmed by the Swedish press release on NobelPrize.org, and for 1958 it was translated from the English motivation. Swedish vitamin names follow the form "C-vitamin" throughout.
6. Second source for every laureate. Wikidata was queried (query 1) for every item with P166 award received = Q44585 (Nobel Prize in Chemistry) and the year of its P585 point in time qualifier. It returned 200 laureate-years for 198 items. All 198 laureates in the API were matched by the Wikidata id the API itself gives (laureate.wikidata.id), and every one has Q44585 with exactly the API's year or years; Wikidata names no holder of the prize that the API does not.
7. Third source. NobelPrize.org's summary page for each year 1901–2025 was fetched (one request per second, script fetch_summary.py) and compared with the cards: every laureate's name (the API's knownName or fullName) appears on that year's page, the eight years without an award say "No Nobel Prize was awarded this year", and the nine prizes whose award decision the API dates to the following year (1914, 1918, 1920, 1921, 1925, 1927, 1938, 1943 and 1944) each say the laureate "received his Nobel Prize one year later". NobelPrize.org is copyrighted and used for verification only.
8. Machine checks. Every card carries Wikidata checks run by the builder (python3 scripts/authored_decks.py build nobel-prize-in-chemistry) against live Wikidata, 548 in all: for every laureate, P166 includes Q44585; the English and the Swedish name on the card is a Wikidata label or alias in that language, or the language-independent "mul" label or alias, where Wikidata has that form (each card's Wikidata evidence says which: 20 names on 14 cards are only mul forms, Marie Curie having no English or Swedish label at all); and Q7186 (Marie Curie) P166 Q38104 and Q48983 (Linus Pauling) P166 Q35637 for the notes. The checks read only truthy property values and cannot see the P585 year qualifier, so the link between year and laureate — the core fact of each card — is verified by query 1 (re-run on 2026-10-04 with the query "P166 years" in Queries: every card's P166-checked items are exactly the items whose Q44585 statement has that card's year), not on every build; it should be re-run before release. Name checks are left out where the card's form is not on Wikidata in that language (mostly the Nobel Foundation's forms with initials or titles, such as "Francis W. Aston" or "Lord Todd"); every such name was confirmed against the API and the NobelPrize.org summary page, and the Swedish ones also against the Swedish Wikipedia table; they are listed in Quality control. The deck was then validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (node scripts/validate_sources.ts nobel-prize-in-chemistry).
9. Study direction. Front to back only: Frederick Sanger and K. Barry Sharpless each appear on two cards, and the backs, lists of names, are not fit to be asked in reverse.
10. Reproduction. The cards were generated from the saved API and Wikidata responses by a script (gen_cards.py) that applies the name decisions in steps 3 and 4 (Back: English and Back: Swedish) and no other transformation (every other name is the API's), joins the names, adds the notes (notes.py, written by hand), writes the evidence of each card from the saved responses and NobelPrize.org pages, and adds the Wikidata checks; a second script (assemble.py) wrote the dossier. The scripts (gen_cards.py, notes.py, compare.py, svlist.py, fetch_summary.py, assemble.py, runq.sh) and all raw responses are kept in a scratch directory outside the repository, so the generation step itself cannot be rerun from the repository; the queries and URLs below are enough to fetch the same data again and the rules above to rebuild the cards.

## Selection

All 117 years from 1901 to 2025 in which the Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded, one card per year, with every laureate of that year: the complete set, nothing chosen. Left out: the eight years with no award (1916, 1917, 1919, 1924, 1933, 1940, 1941 and 1942), since a card for them would have no laureate to learn; and the 2026 prize, which NobelPrize.org says is announced on 7 October 2026, after this deck was made on 4 October 2026. The year is the prize year, not the year it was awarded: the nine prizes reserved and awarded the following year (1914, 1918, 1920, 1921, 1925, 1927, 1938, 1943 and 1944) are on the card of the year they are for (Fritz Haber's 1918 prize, awarded in 1919, is on the card 1918). The notes say what each prize was for and, where a laureate won another Nobel Prize, which; they do not give the laureates' countries or affiliations (several laureates had more than one), and they do not mention that Richard Kuhn (1938) and Adolf Butenandt (1939) were made by the German authorities to decline their prizes and later received the diploma and medal: the API, the content source, records both prizes as received, and NobelPrize.org, which tells the story (for Kuhn), is a verification source only.

## Queries

**All Nobel Prizes in Chemistry, by year (saved as prizes.json)** (Nobel Prize API 2.1 (api.nobelprize.org): Nobel Prizes in Chemistry and chemistry laureates (nobelPrizes and laureates endpoints))

```
curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o prizes.json "https://api.nobelprize.org/2.1/nobelPrizes?nobelPrizeCategory=che&limit=200&sort=asc&format=json"
```

**All chemistry laureates, with names, prizes, Wikidata ids (saved as laureates.json)** (Nobel Prize API 2.1 (api.nobelprize.org): Nobel Prizes in Chemistry and chemistry laureates (nobelPrizes and laureates endpoints))

```
curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o laureates.json "https://api.nobelprize.org/2.1/laureates?nobelPrizeCategory=che&limit=300&format=json"
```

**The API terms of use (CC0)** (Nobel Prize API 2.1 (api.nobelprize.org): Nobel Prizes in Chemistry and chemistry laureates (nobelPrizes and laureates endpoints))

```
curl -sL -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o terms.html "https://www.nobelprize.org/about/terms-of-use-for-api-nobelprize-org-and-data-nobelprize-org/"
```

**How every SPARQL query below was run (runq.sh <name>, e.g. "runq.sh q1"): the query saved as a file (q1.rq, q2.rq) in the scratch directory and sent to the Wikidata Query Service; expanded for q1:** (Wikidata)

```
curl -s -G https://query.wikidata.org/sparql --data-urlencode query@<scratch>/q1.rq -H "Accept: application/sparql-results+json" -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o <scratch>/q1.json
```

**Query 1 (q1.rq): every holder of the Nobel Prize in Chemistry with the year and English, Swedish and language-independent labels and the Swedish Wikipedia article** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?laureate ?enLabel ?svLabel ?mulLabel ?year ?svwiki WHERE {
  ?laureate p:P166 ?award .
  ?award ps:P166 wd:Q44585 ; pq:P585 ?date .
  BIND(YEAR(?date) AS ?year)
  OPTIONAL { ?laureate rdfs:label ?enLabel . FILTER(LANG(?enLabel) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?laureate rdfs:label ?svLabel . FILTER(LANG(?svLabel) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?laureate rdfs:label ?mulLabel . FILTER(LANG(?mulLabel) = "mul") }
  OPTIONAL { ?svwiki schema:about ?laureate ; schema:isPartOf <https://sv.wikipedia.org/> . }
}
ORDER BY ?year ?enLabel
```

**Query 2 (q2.rq): the English, Swedish and "mul" labels and aliases of every holder of the prize, to see which names on the cards Wikidata has** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?laureate ?kind ?text WHERE {
  ?laureate p:P166 ?award .
  ?award ps:P166 wd:Q44585 .
  { ?laureate rdfs:label ?text . BIND("label" AS ?kind) } UNION { ?laureate skos:altLabel ?text . BIND("alias" AS ?kind) }
  FILTER(LANG(?text) IN ("en", "sv", "mul"))
}
```

**Wikidata's licence** (Wikidata)

```
curl -sL -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o wikidata-licensing.html "https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Wikidata:Licensing"
```

**The summary page of every prize year 1901–2025 (fetch_summary.py), one request per second with the User-Agent above; script and style elements and tags stripped, entities unescaped, whitespace collapsed, and the text from the second occurrence of "The Nobel Prize in Chemistry <year>" kept** (NobelPrize.org: the summary page of every Nobel Prize in Chemistry year, the 2026 announcement dates and the Swedish press release of 2021)

```
For each year y from 1901 to 2025, one GET per second (Python urllib):

```

```
curl -sL -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o nobelprize-terms.html "https://www.nobelprize.org/about/terms-of-use/"
```

## Quality control

6 rounds, 22 findings: 17 fixed, 0 rejected after checking, 5 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (548 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Completeness and correctness against the sources; agreement between the Nobel Prize API, Wikidata, NobelPrize.org and the Swedish Wikipedia; Wikidata machine checks (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 117 cards

The API's 125 prize years (117 with an award, 8 without) and 198 laureates (200 laureate-years) were matched one by one against Wikidata's P166 Q44585 statements with their P585 years and against NobelPrize.org's summary page for every year. The laureates and years agree in all three, with no exception; the eight years without an award and the nine prizes awarded a year later agree between the API and NobelPrize.org. All 548 Wikidata checks passed in the build (python3 scripts/authored_decks.py build nobel-prize-in-chemistry, 2026-10-04). No independent review round has been run yet. The P166 checks confirm that each laureate received the prize but cannot see the year; the year of each card rests on the API, NobelPrize.org and query 1 (the P585 years), as method step 8 (Machine checks) says.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1958-sanger | The API's Swedish motivation for 1958 is "för deras insatser rörande bassekvensbestämning i nukleinsyror", the 1980 motivation of Gilbert and Sanger, not a translation of the 1958 English motivation ("for his work on the structure of proteins, especially that of insulin", confirmed by NobelPrize.org and by the Swedish Wikipedia table's translation). | The Swedish note was translated from the English motivation: "Proteiners struktur, särskilt insulinets."
